<reflection>
The previous experiment with added initial product (0.2 M) successfully probed product-dependent steps, further separating deactivation mechanisms (M16, M15, M14, M20, M11) as the best fits, with NLL values around -60. The aim to discriminate using product was achieved, as seen by the widened gap between the deactivation group and simpler reversible mechanisms (NLL ~ -42). However, within the deactivation group, multiple mechanisms remain with very similar NLLs, indicating continued uncertainty. The need now is to design an experiment that discriminates among these top deactivation mechanisms and also tests against dimerization (M3) and other plausible candidates.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
I propose lowering the substrate concentration to 1.0 M while keeping catalyst at 0.01 M and product at 0 M. This reduces the formation of the catalyst-substrate complex (catS), which will differentially affect deactivation pathways: mechanisms that deactivate catS (e.g., M14, M16, M17, M20) should show a relatively smaller deactivation effect compared to those that deactivate free catalyst (e.g., M9, M10, M11, M12). Additionally, this condition probes saturation behavior and substrate inhibition (M7) and dimerization (M3) under a different regime. The design is effective because it targets multiple mechanistic classes simultaneously, avoids extreme conditions, and introduces a new variation in substrate concentration not yet explored, thereby providing broad discrimination power across the remaining plausible set.
</hypothesis>
